name: Baby Shit Brown
lede: Baby Shit Brown is a mustard-brown named, bluntly, for the color of an infant's stool, one of several near-identical names the 2010 xkcd color survey gave to this stretch of yellow-brown.

sections.title: A crowd name for a plain comparison
sections.body:
The name comes from Randall Munroe's 2010 xkcd color survey, where visitors typed a word next to a swatch and the most common label for each cluster of clicks won [1]. Who typed it first is undocumented; the survey records only the winning name [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the same patch as a deep yellow, about 1.8 units off, the closest match of any of this cluster's names, with Munsell notation 5.0Y 6.0/8.9 [1].

The vote also produced near-duplicates for closely related shades, including [[baby-poo|Baby Poo]] and [[baby-poop|Baby Poop]], all naming the same comparison rather than a dye or a place [1]. The closest look-alikes in our data are [[dark-mustard|Dark Mustard]] and [[brown-yellow|Brown-Yellow]], both within 2.4 units [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, finds this mustard-brown in 105 of them, about 0.44 percent, more common than 59 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1700s, at 1.6 times the expected rate for that century (25 of 3,449 paintings from then), and inside a painting it is almost always an accent, 77 percent of the time, by lightness rank rather than raw area [2].

Luis Egidio Meléndez is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 5 of his 39 works here, 7.3 times the baseline rate for the museums those works come from [2]. It is also over-represented in paintings from India, at 5.1 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest match in our archive is dated 1403, by Gherardo Starnina, 607 years before the name itself appears in 2010; our archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first [2].
